title: Smoky split pea and cabbage stew

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is a plain cupboard or garden item: split peas, tinned tomatoes, stock, vegetables and spices.

supermarket.reason: Yellow split peas, caraway seeds and white cabbage are all everyday Tesco items at low prices.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a lidded casserole, a knife and a board.

works.reason: 250g split peas with 1.2 litres of stock, a tin of tomatoes and half a cabbage, simmered for an hour, gives a thick stew that comfortably serves four.

honest_times.reason: Twenty minutes is fair for chopping two onions, three carrots and garlic and shredding half a cabbage, and the 70 cook minutes match the 10 + 1 + 40 + 20 in the steps.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning is used and nothing unlisted appears; the step's 'paprika' clearly means the listed smoked paprika.

seasonal_feel.reason: A warming cabbage and split pea stew suits late February, and half a cabbage is a main component rather than a garnish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, clear British English a beginner can follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: Pulses and plenty of vegetables make a filling, wholesome family dinner.
